summary: No trades on the XFA today, and that was the right call. Pre-market wanted the Asia SMT and the 4hr bearish gap to deliver into 167, price ran lower without giving a clean NY entry, and you sat on your hands instead of chasing. Morning check-in was on time at 9:29 with the same 167 plan, and the EOD card matches Notion and the journal post. The options short you logged yesterday (QQQ 670 put bought at $2.63 on Nov 4, sold at $13.25 today) is the real win of the day at about 5.04R, and AB called it a beautiful trade.
trade: No Trades · NY-AM · XFA · NT · pre-market bias short toward 167 off Asia SMT inside a 4hr bearish gap · no funded entry · separate Robinhood QQQ $670 put 11/12 from yesterday closed today at ~5.04R (buy $2.63 / sell $13.25, $270 full risk).
rule: Tomorrow, if the A+ futures setup never prints, sit again the same way you did today. Do not add a second idea on the XFA just because the options already paid, and do not size up options because one hit.

good: No XFA trade when there was no clean NY entry — you wrote you did not FOMO and the EOD says you sat on your hands.
Morning plan (167 / Asia SMT / 4hr gap) matched pre-market Notion and the charts at 9:24–9:26.
Morning check-in on time at 9:29 AM ET (charts opened 9:25), before the 9:30 deadline.
Options risk was capped at the premium you were okay losing ($270), and you took the win instead of turning it into revenge size.
Journal post, Notion TALK, and EOD all agree: no funded trades today; options was yesterday's entry.
fix: The morning risk screenshot was a Tradovate MNQ chart/DOM with PDLL visible, not a clear risk-settings panel. Post the actual loss-limit / trade-limit screen so the check-in proves the rule, not just that a chart was open.

Options still sits outside the NQ-futures-only rule. Keep journaling it (you did), but decide explicitly whether Robinhood options are allowed in your process or a one-off, so it does not quietly become a second book after a win.

You closed the QQQ put the same day after planning to hold until next week Thursday. That is fine if the thesis was delivered, but write the exit rule next time so 'hold till next week' is not just hope.

questions.q: You planned to hold the QQQ 670 put until next week Thursday because the DOL was 1k+ points away, then sold today at $13.25. What specifically told you the idea was done?
questions.answer: want me hit my drama quitting at Target that's what I knew it was basically done that's why I just closed it but I told Brock where should I live or whatever because I was afraid that I don't limit order or sell limit put a sale limit in a cells I felt like we were just reject off of it hard and then go higher but then we ended up just continuing to shoot lower I guess seeing that much money made me nervous and not nervous well actually I wasn't really nerves I was pretty excited but could have I lost that like 200 300 bucks because of grock told me to limit it to limit like 13.25 and it went all day till like $16 then I was like bro
questions.reply: You closed because you felt the idea was done and locked the win at the 13.25 limit instead of riding open risk, which is solid when size was already capped at the premium you could lose. Watching it run to 16 afterward is normal FOMO after a ~5R day, not proof the exit was wrong. Next time write the exit level before the thrill hits so the limit is a plan, not a scramble mid-move.

questions.q: Pre-market and the morning check-in both wanted 167. On the 5m at 9:26 price had already swept AS.L near 28,175 — what would an A+ XFA short have needed after that, that never printed?
You told Bibz you need a month of discipline around accounts/evals. What is the one concrete rule for that month so a win like today's options does not turn into 'I can buy another eval'?
